sections.h2: What sets the Newark market apart
sections.html:
Newark is in New Castle County, about 8 miles west-southwest of Wilmington and 28 miles southwest of Philadelphia, just east of the Maryland line. The 2020 Census counted 30,601 residents with a median age of 24.2. That low number reflects the University of Delaware, whose campus sits beside Main Street, the commercial center.

For a seller, the student population is the main fact about the local housing market. It creates steady rental demand, and it also brings a set of city rules that decide what a house can be used for after you sell it.

I-95 and Delaware routes 2, 72, 273, 279 and 896 all serve Newark. The Newark rail station is on the Northeast Corridor with SEPTA and Amtrak service, and DART First State and DART Connect buses use the Newark Transit Hub.

Rail access draws commuters and students who live without a car. Houses within walking distance of the station or Main Street tend to attract a different crowd than houses on the outskirts, so describe where yours sits and let buyers decide what that is worth to them.

An annual rental permit is required for non-owner-occupied property leased to tenants, and also for an owner-occupied home that rents rooms to more than two unrelated people. A change of ownership, even between relatives, calls for an updated rental license application.

Student homes get the most specific treatment. The city defines one as a single-family detached dwelling occupied by three post-secondary students who are unrelated by blood or adoption, and it sets these conditions:

  • No more than three people may live in a student home.
  • It must sit farther from any other student home than ten times the required lot width for a single-family house in that district.
  • Rentals that already held permits when the ordinance was adopted count toward that distance.
  • Thirty-three listed subdivisions and some listed streets are outside the definition.

Zoning limits non-owner-occupied single-family rentals to three unrelated occupants in the RH, RT, RS, RD and RR districts, and four in RM. Some deeds set lower limits, so read yours. An investor who wants to keep renting your house, particularly as a student home, has to check the distance rule before making an offer.

sections.h2: Inspection and exterior rules for rentals
sections.html:
The Code Enforcement Division requires exterior and common-area inspections for rentals, and rental units get an annual inspection. Ask the division which inspections apply to your unit, since interior visits are described as voluntary in some places and required in others.

The city lists these upkeep rules for rental properties:

  • Refuse cans of 20 or 32 gallons, labeled with the address, with tight lids.
  • Curbside refuse under 40 pounds, set out no earlier than 6:00 p.m. the day before collection.
  • Weed and grass notices once growth passes 10 inches.
  • Snow and ice cleared from the sidewalk within 24 hours, leaving a path at least three feet wide.

Leases longer than 30 days are required, and an occupant posting must hang inside the unit. Code Enforcement is at 220 South Main Street, phone (302) 366-7000.

The city real estate tax rate for 2026 to 2027 is $0.2464 per $100 of assessed value. Bills are issued after July 1 and are due by September 30 to avoid a penalty. New Castle County's Assessment Office sets the assessed value, which drives both the city tax and the school tax, and assessments are listed as of April 1.

If your mortgage company pays taxes from escrow, the bill you receive is for information only. Past-due notices go out quarterly. The city Finance Department answers tax questions at (302) 366-7000.

Newark runs its own electric department, serving about 12,800 customers, and a water system serving about 33,000. Because the city is the utility, a final meter reading and a payoff figure matter at settlement. Ask for both a few days before closing so nothing is left on your account when the deed is recorded.

Grass, weeds, refuse and snow are enforced at the city level too, so a vacant house still needs someone to mind the exterior until the sale closes.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and closing in Delaware
sections.html:
Delaware's realty transfer tax is normally 4 percent, made up of 2.5 percent for the state and 1.5 percent for the county or municipality. The law divides it equally between seller and buyer. A first-time buyer can reduce the buyer's share by 0.5 percent of up to $400,000, which is worth up to $2,000.

A seller of a one to four unit home must give the written disclosure report before an offer. An attorney must run the settlement, since the state Supreme Court's 2000 Mid-Atlantic Settlement Services decision and its 2006 order treat closings as the practice of law.

We buy Newark houses as-is, including houses with rental history. Offers are not promised until we see the property.

Collect your deed, the latest city tax bill, the county assessed value, your final utility figures and the completed disclosure report. Choose the closing attorney early, because the attorney opens the title search and will ask for these papers first. If the house is a rental, add the permit, the last inspection result and the lease. Having everything in one folder lets a buyer make a firm offer faster and cuts down on questions in the last week before closing.

sections.h2: Selling a house with tenants or rental history
sections.html:
A sale of a rented house raises questions an owner-occupied sale does not. Sort these out before you accept a closing date.

  • Confirm whether your rental permit is current and ask Code Enforcement at (302) 366-7000 about the discontinuation form if the rental is ending.
  • Find out what the lease says about notice and showings, and give tenants written notice for each visit.
  • Tell the buyer whether the house has been used as a student home, since that status affects what they can do with it.
  • Keep copies of the last passed inspection and any notices from the city.

A cash buyer who wants a vacant house will usually ask when the tenants leave, so a clear move-out date helps. If a buyer plans to keep renting, the updated rental license application must be filed after the ownership change.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit to sell a Newark rental?
faqs.a: You need a valid permit while the house is rented, and any ownership change calls for an updated rental license application, even between related parties. Contact Code Enforcement at (302) 366-7000 for the discontinuation form if the rental ends.

faqs.q: What is a student home in Newark?
faqs.a: It is a single-family detached dwelling occupied by three post-secondary students unrelated by blood or adoption. A student home must meet a distance requirement from other student homes and may have no more than three occupants.

faqs.q: When is Newark city property tax due?
faqs.a: Bills are issued after July 1 and must be paid by September 30 to avoid a penalty. For 2026 to 2027 the city rate is $0.2464 per $100 of assessed value.

faqs.q: Who sets assessed values for Newark properties?
faqs.a: New Castle County's Assessment Office sets them, and the Board of Assessment Review decides appeals. Call the county at (302) 395-5520 for appeal forms.

faqs.q: Is a lawyer required to close a Newark house sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Delaware requires an attorney to conduct real estate settlements, following the state Supreme Court's 2000 Mid-Atlantic Settlement Services decision and its 2006 order.
